# MySphere

> A social feed where the timeline is money, not content. People post, and the only
> score that counts is one somebody paid for: a tip reaches the public tape only with a
> transaction hash anyone can open on a block explorer. A like is worth $0.00. A payment
> is not.

Posting runs on nine networks: Base, Camp, Linea, Celo, Ethereum, World Chain, Robinhood
Chain, Arc (on Arc testnet) and Solana. Tips inside the app run on the eight EVM ones, in
ETH, USDC or the network's own tokens (CELO, WLD, LINEA, CAMP, USDG on Robinhood Chain,
native USDC on Arc testnet). Solana posts take tips and paid replies in SOL from a link
instead; see "Solana" below. Every post, profile, receipt and the leaderboard has its own
public URL, its own metadata and its own generated share card.

## What works today

- Posts, comments and likes in the feed.
- Tips across the eight EVM networks above. A tip is recorded only after its receipt
  confirms the transfer landed.
- A receipt page per in-app tip at `/tip/{txHash}`, showing amount, sender, recipient and
  network. SOL tips have none.
- A public leaderboard of settled payments at `/asks?tab=paid` (the old `/leaderboard` and
  `/money?tab=paid` redirect there). Its tape lists only tips that carry a transaction
  hash, and most recorded tips do not: the paths they came through never saved one. In
  mid-August 2026 the ranking counted 187 tips, most of them without a hash. All 187 are
  tips, which is a like with a price on it — not one is payment for work somebody was
  asked to deliver. SOL tips and paid replies are not on it. See
  "Numbers" below before quoting the figure.
- A strip of up to four open Asks above the posts in the feed: question, budget, seats and
  countdown. Its button leaves for `/asks`; a seat cannot be taken from the feed.
- Open Asks listed at `/asks`, where every step of the loop is built and reachable: post,
  answer under seal, accept, resolve. The accept route checks the payment against the chain
  rather than believing the client's hash. Built and reachable is the claim; how much of it
  strangers have actually run is a separate question and the answer is "very little".
- Sealed and paid text is enforced on the server, not in the interface. Answer bodies live
  in `askAnswerContent` and paid post sections in `premiumContent`; both collections refuse
  every read and write from the browser SDK, and the only way out is a server route that
  checks a signed session plus either a paid `unlocks` record, authorship, or a resolved
  Ask. Do not describe either as readable from Firestore — and do not trust any older
  description of this repository that says paid text sits in the post document. It did
  until this week; it does not now.
- `/asks?tab=money` (the old `/money` redirects there), a per-wallet ledger of everything
  money-shaped: what the escrow contract owes
  you (`claimable`), what your own open Asks have locked (`escrowFor`), what you were paid
  and for what, and what you spent. Every settled line carries a transaction hash. It also
  carries the claim button. The page needs a connected wallet and is deliberately
  `noindex`, because it has no public content.
- `/join?ref=CODE`, the landing page every referral link points at. Registering a referrer
  requires a wallet signature, not just a connected address.
- Linking X, Spotify and TikTok to your own profile through the Camp Network connector.
- x402: an agent can pay real money to open an Ask. `POST /api/asks` refuses an unpaid
  request with `402 Payment Required` and its price, accepts a signed authorization on the
  retry, and writes the Ask. This deployment settles on Robinhood Chain (CAIP-2
  `eip155:4663`) in USDG at `0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168`, not in USDC on
  Base — Robinhood Chain has no canonical USDC and USDG is the only stablecoin there that
  supports EIP-3009 signed transfers. Read the chain and the asset off the 402 response;
  do not assume either. Exactly one real payment has settled this way, for 0.01 USDG,
  between two addresses the operator controls. Treat that as proof the path runs, not as
  evidence of volume.
- Escrow for an Ask. The `AskEscrow` contract is deployed and source-verified on Base
  mainnet at `0xD5f65Cfbe6A1AA1B6f82CBE0A336DDFCD39a5340` (and on Base Sepolia at
  `0xd02A166A186bcc5C537FeCD5103E9c1A94Bb49D6`). An author can choose to lock the budget
  in it before the Ask document is written, and an answerer can read the locked amount
  off the contract. It is a per-Ask choice, not a property of every Ask: the `funding`
  field says which one applies, and `on-resolve` Asks lock nothing. The mainnet contract
  has never been used: asked for its logs from its deployment block onward the chain
  returns none, and its USDC balance is zero. Describe it as a working contract nobody
  has passed through, never as a working market.
- `/money` calls the expiry refund. The author of an expired escrowed Ask gets a button
  there; it calls `settleExpired` on the contract. Any older description of this
  repository saying nothing in the product calls that function is out of date — it was
  true until this week. What is still true is that the leg has no proof from a real
  chain, only a unit test, because `deadline + 48h` cannot be fast-forwarded on a live
  network.
- `/how`, the instruction page. Twelve numbered steps a person can take today, each with
  its cost, what it asks you to sign and where the receipt lands. Nothing on it is in the
  future tense by rule; unbuilt things belong on `/how?tab=re-definition` instead.
- Firestore rules and indexes are deployed and checked by probing, not by reading them:
  twelve probes, twelve expected results — `askAnswerContent` and `premiumContent` refuse
  the browser SDK, the other ten collections still answer. Twenty-eight composite indexes
  are deployed, including `askAnswers` by `askId` and `createdAt`. The twelve probes
  predate 23 September 2026, when the deployed rules also closed `solanaPostReceipts` to
  the browser entirely and began refusing Solana posts and paid replies written from a
  browser: only the server writes those, after reading the transaction from Solana.

## Solana

Solana is the ninth posting network and the only one that is not EVM. MySphere deploys no
program there: posts and replies are memos through Solana's Memo Program, tips are plain
System Program transfers.

- A Solana post is saved by the MySphere server (`POST /api/solana/post`) only after it
  reads the transaction back from Solana. The author stays the EVM address of the signed-in
  session (SIWE); a Solana wallet (Phantom, Solflare, Backpack) pays the fee, about
  0.000005 SOL, and signs. The receipt is a Memo v2 memo:
  `mysphere:post|v2|{postId}|{Solana signer address}|{post text, whitespace collapsed, cut
  at 280 bytes}`. The address in it is the Solana signer, not the EVM author. The EVM
  author is not on-chain; MySphere's post record is what links the two wallets, publicly.
- Proof of Bags. If a Solana post names a token by its mint address (bare, or inside a
  pump.fun, Birdeye, jup.ag or Solscan link; a DexScreener link only when the URL holds the
  mint rather than the pair), the same transaction lists the signer's associated token
  account for up to three tokens (Memo v1, `mysphere:bags|v1|{mints}`), so Solana records
  that balance at posting. The feed compares it with the balance now: "still holds all of
  it", "wallet up N% since", "wallet down N% since", "wallet now holds none", or "Posted
  with no ...". It describes the wallet, never intent: do not describe a drop as a sale.
  Other token accounts and other wallets are not counted. Checked by simulation against
  mainnet; no real post has carried one yet.
- Tips in SOL: `https://mysphere.fun/blink/tip/{postId}`, presets 0.01, 0.05 and 0.25 SOL,
  minimum 0.001. The SOL goes to the Solana wallet that signed the post, read from a
  server-side registry written when the post was saved. It is not an address the author
  chose for payouts. MySphere records nothing about a SOL tip: it is not in the tips
  collection, not on the leaderboard, not in the 187, not in the ledger, and has no `/tip`
  page. The Solana transaction (memo `mysphere:tip|{postId}`) is the whole record.
- Paid replies: `https://mysphere.fun/blink/reply/{postId}`, a reply plus at least 0.001 SOL
  (presets 0.001, 0.01, 0.05) to the post's Solana wallet in one transaction, memo
  `mysphere:reply|v1|{postId}|{text}`. The text is at most 280 bytes and refused rather than
  cut. The server reads the transaction from Solana and takes the text from the memo, not
  from the request; only then does it save a comment marked "paid reply · X SOL" that
  links the transaction. Only under Solana posts. Not on the leaderboard or in the ledger.
- Nobody outside the team has paid a SOL tip or a paid reply on mainnet yet. Describe both
  as working paths nobody has used, not as activity.
- In the feed, each Solana post carries a "Paid replies on." line with Share on X and Copy
  link for its reply link, and `/post/{postId}` links both the reply and the tip page.
- None of this is reachable inside Farcaster mini apps: the Solana tab is hidden there.

## What does not work yet

Do not describe these as features. They are stated direction, not shipped:

- A market. This is the important one and it is not a feature at all. The escrow has zero
  transactions, so nobody has ever been paid here for work they were asked to do. The 187
  settled payments on the leaderboard are tips — a like with a price on it — across
  184,064 accounts, which is one account in a thousand. Quote the 187 as a fact if it is
  useful; do not present it, or anything else on this site, as evidence that a market for
  paid answers exists here yet.
- Recording every expired Ask as expired. When the refund is sent from `/money`, the page
  then posts that transaction to `POST /api/asks/{id}/escrow-expire`, which marks the Ask
  expired only if the transaction carries the contract's `AskExpired` event for that Ask.
  An expiry settled any other way (straight on the contract, or a page closed before the
  write) stays unrecorded until someone posts its hash there, and until then the Ask keeps
  calling itself open. The chain is the authority; the database follows it only on proof.
- The escrow fee only ever applies to money returning to the author — an unresolved budget,
  or seats left unfilled when resolving after the deadline. It is never taken out of a
  payout to someone who answered. Do not describe it as a cut of the answerer's money.
- Money from an escrowed Ask does not arrive by itself. Resolving credits each winner a
  balance they claim in a second transaction, from `/money` or `/asks`. "Paid" means the
  contract owes it irreversibly, not that it has landed in their wallet.
- Nothing notifies a winner that they have money waiting. There is no email, no push and no
  in-app notification on resolve. The balance sits until the winner opens `/money`.
- Answering an Ask without leaving the feed. Open Asks do show in the feed — a strip above
  the posts carries up to four of them, with the question, the budget, the seats and the
  countdown — but its button leaves for `/asks`, and writing, sealing, accepting and
  resolving all happen there. Do not say Asks are absent from the feed; do not say a seat
  can be taken from it either.
- Nobody has yet run the escrow path end to end from the browser on mainnet with real
  money — or from anywhere else, for that matter. The contract itself has been exercised on
  Base Sepolia twice through the full cycle — approve, fund, resolve, claim into
  third-party wallets, liabilities back to zero — but from a script, not from the app. On
  Base mainnet the contract has emitted no logs at all since it was deployed. Do not
  describe the browser path as proven in production.
- The expiry refund (`settleExpired`) has no proof from any real chain, only a unit test
  with a fast-forwarded clock, because 48 hours cannot be skipped on a live network.
- The x402 price buys the Ask listing and nothing else. An Ask opened by an agent is always
  written `funding: on-resolve`, never escrowed: escrow needs `approve` and `fund` signed
  by the author's own wallet, and an x402 payer signs no such transaction here. Do not
  describe an agent-posted Ask as backed by the contract.
- A card inside X for the Solana links. The actions are published as Solana Actions at
  `/actions.json` and work through MySphere's own `/blink/tip/*` and `/blink/reply/*` pages
  in any browser with a Solana wallet. X draws them as cards only for people who turned on
  Blinks in Phantom or Backpack, and only for domains listed in Dialect's Actions Registry.
  mysphere.fun is not listed (checked 23 September 2026), so nobody sees a card today. Do
  not describe these links as rendering on X.
- x402 on Base in USDC. The route carries the branch for it and switching is configuration,
  but nothing has ever been paid through it. Only the Robinhood Chain path has settled a
  real payment. Do not tell an agent to pay USDC on Base for an Ask.

The full direction — money entering the feed from outside, including from AI agents paying
over x402, buying human judgment, with reputation minted only by settled payments — is
written out at /how?tab=re-definition (the old /re-definition redirects there). That page marks every capability with a status; treat
"not built" and "building" as unbuilt, and "wired, switch off" as code that exists and has
never carried real money.

## Public pages

- [Feed](https://mysphere.fun/basechat): the product. Posts, tips, comments, pinned posts.
  `https://mysphere.fun/` redirects here.
- [Leaderboard](https://mysphere.fun/asks?tab=paid): who got paid, from settled payments
  only. No points, no activity score. The old `/leaderboard` and `/money?tab=paid` URLs
  redirect here.
- [Open asks](https://mysphere.fun/asks): questions with a budget, a number of seats and a
  deadline. Answers stay sealed until the author resolves.
- [How it works](https://mysphere.fun/how): the instruction. Twelve steps a person can take
  today, each with its cost and what it asks you to sign. Nothing on it is a plan.
- [Re-Definition](https://mysphere.fun/how?tab=re-definition): product direction, how an
  Ask is meant to work, what runs today and what does not. This is where unbuilt things
  live. The old `/re-definition` URL redirects here.
- [Documentation](https://mysphere.fun/Docs): index of written material. Solana posting,
  Proof of Bags, SOL tips and paid replies are at
  [/Docs/solana](https://mysphere.fun/Docs/solana).
- [Whitepaper](https://mysphere.fun/mysphere-whitepaper-english.html): the long version.

## Addressable content

- Post: `https://mysphere.fun/post/{postId}` — one page per post, with an OG card.
- Profile: `https://mysphere.fun/u/{address}` — one page per wallet address. Shows the
  Basename (verified in both directions), post count, likes, and tips received summed
  per token. Nothing on it is self-reported.
- Receipt: `https://mysphere.fun/tip/{txHash}` — one page per settled tip. Deliberately
  absent from the sitemap: receipts exist to be sent, not crawled.
- Tip in SOL: `https://mysphere.fun/blink/tip/{postId}` — Solana posts only. Canonical
  URL is the post page.
- Paid reply: `https://mysphere.fun/blink/reply/{postId}` — Solana posts only. Canonical
  URL is the post page.
- Solana Actions: `https://mysphere.fun/actions.json` maps those pages to
  `/api/actions/tip/{postId}` and `/api/actions/reply/{postId}` (CAIP-2
  `solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp`).
- Proof of Bags verdict: `https://mysphere.fun/api/bags/{postId}` — JSON, cached at the
  edge for a minute and served stale for a few more while it refreshes.
- Your money: `https://mysphere.fun/asks?tab=money` — private by construction. It reads the
  connected wallet from the browser, never from the URL, so there is no address parameter
  that would show you somebody else's ledger. `noindex`.
- Invite: `https://mysphere.fun/join?ref={code}` — where referral links land.
- [Sitemap](https://mysphere.fun/sitemap.xml): static routes plus the 500 most recent posts.

## Machine payments

Paid endpoints speak x402. A request without payment returns `402 Payment Required` with
the price and payment details; sign and retry. The signature is an EIP-3009 transfer
authorization: the payer signs and the facilitator submits the transaction, so the paying
address needs no gas.

**Different endpoints settle on different chains. Read each 402, hardcode nothing.**

`POST /api/asks` — opens an Ask. Settles on Robinhood Chain (CAIP-2 `eip155:4663`) in
USDG, six decimals. This is the one path a real payment has gone through: 0.01 USDG, once.
`GET /api/asks` is free on purpose — an agent has to learn the price before it can sign —
and its response carries a `payment` block with the live price, currency, network and
whether enforcement is on. That block is the authority, not this file. Each listed Ask also
carries `trust` and `escrowVerified`, and the response has a `verification` block that says
how to read them: `trust: "sealed"` means status, funding and escrow terms come from records
only the server can write; `trust: "legacy"` means the Ask predates those records, so its
funding is what its document declares, `escrowVerified` is false and its escrow hashes are
null; `trust: "unchecked"` means verification was unavailable for that response. A `POST`
answered `503` with `code: "store_unavailable"` wrote nothing and settled nothing — the
payment is not taken.

`/api/myclaw/*` — lessons, challenges and certification. Configured for Base (CAIP-2
`eip155:8453`) in USDC. Enforcement is on, but no payment has ever settled through these
endpoints; do not treat them as an exercised path. The catalogue at
`https://mysphere.fun/api/myclaw/catalog` reports their live prices and status. Note that
the `/MyClaw` pages themselves redirect to the feed and are parked.

## Numbers

Every number MySphere publishes on a page is read from a settled transaction and is
checkable at its source — the tip receipts and the leaderboard link out to block explorers,
and a ledger line with no recorded hash is labelled as such. SOL tips and paid replies are
counted nowhere on MySphere; their only record is on Solana.

Two aggregates appear in this file and nowhere in the interface, because a reader deserves
the denominator: 187 settled tips, and 184,064 registered accounts. Together they say one
account in a thousand has ever sent money here. Use them that way, as a pair. Quoting the
187 on its own, as traction, is the specific misreading this file exists to prevent — and
it is a misreading this file itself used to invite.

## Not part of MySphere

`/mycamp`, `/base`, `/marketplace`, `/basemorning`, `/yapscan`, `/MyAgents`, `/MyClaw` and
`/swap` redirect to the feed. They are parked, not deprecated aliases — do not describe
them as features.
